kidney.reason: Kidney L/R dropped: Z-Anatomy's kidney is credited to a CC BY-NC 4.0 model (lissiecowley); provenance of the shandons-repo copy is not verifiable, so it is omitted to keep the build CC BY-SA clean. Use a HuBMAP (CC BY 4.0) or BodyParts3D kidney if one is wanted.

renalPelvis.reason: Renal pelvis L/R dropped: same source family as the dropped kidney, and its upstream licence cannot be verified, so it is omitted to keep the build CC BY-SA clean. Ureters and urethra stay in 'bladder'.

lymphNodes.reason: Regional lymph node meshes in the lymphoid layer are outside the requested scope (spleen, thymus, tonsils only).

notMapped.layers: muscles.glb, vessels.glb and skin.glb are not mapped here (out of scope). Great-vessel stubs (aorta, pulmonary trunk, venae cavae) live in vessels.glb, not organs.glb, so the heart group holds chambers, papillary muscles and valve leaflets only.
notMapped.brain: No whole-brain mesh exists in organs.glb, so there is no body 'brain' group; the brain is handled by brain-map.json (nerves.glb).
notMapped.ileum: No ileum mesh exists; small_intestine holds duodenum and jejunum.
notMapped.rectum: No rectum mesh exists; large_intestine holds ascending, transverse, descending and sigmoid colon, taeniae and appendix.

notes: Keys are sanitize(name) = name.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/g, ''); nodesRaw carries the original names index-aligned with nodes. Lymphoid names use Blender dot style (Palatine tonsil.l becomes Palatinetonsill).

A group has one layer. Laryngeal cartilages and the hyoid are skeleton-layer meshes, so they form their own 'larynx' group (layer skeleton); the epiglottis, trachea and bronchi are in 'airway' (layer organs).

Extra groups beyond the brief: larynx, endocrine, mouth_throat, thymus, tonsils (needed so every skeleton, organ and lymphoid node in scope lands in exactly one group). Parathyroids sit in 'thyroid'. Ureters and urethra sit in 'bladder'; the renal pelvis is dropped (see `dropped`).

Hip-joint capsule, ligaments and labrum are assigned to the leg groups; ankle ligaments to the foot groups; wrist and carpal ligaments to the hand groups; shoulder-joint ligaments to shoulder_girdle; sacro-iliac and pubic ligaments to pelvis.
Unsided names were resolved to L or R by twin lookup (for example 'Ulnopisiform ligament' is R because 'Ulnopisiform ligament L' exists).

The spine and ribcage are split into one region per vertebra, disc and rib. Each intervertebral disc region joins the disc with its nucleus pulposus; each rib joins the bone with its costal cartilage (ribs 11 and 12 have none). `spine` and `ribcage` keep the sacrum, coccyx, sternum and the ligaments, so their ids still work. Regions sharing a `pivot` key take one node origin (the joint centre of the family), so the family scales and breathes as one.
